title: Store test session cache lives only in tests/conftest.py, not per module
answers: why was cached_db overridden in tests/store/tracking/conftest.py
where to define the sqlite cache for tracking store tests
module-scoped cached_db fixture removed tracking tests
shared artifact_folder path in tracking tests
body:
Convention: Tracking store tests reuse the session-scoped cached_db from tests/conftest.py. Do not redefine cached_db per module in tests/store/tracking/conftest.py.
Why: A module-scoped override repeated migrations for every module and embedded a shared relative artifact path ("artifact_folder"), which conflicts with per-test artifact isolation.
Fix pattern: Delete the local override and let the store fixture in tests/store/tracking/conftest.py:store consume the root cache, passing artifacts under the test's tmp_path.
Constraints: If a module genuinely needs a different database state, add a fixture under its own name rather than shadowing cached_db.
applies: tests/store/tracking and other test modules that depend on the cached_db fixture.
says: Tracking store tests run slowly because database setup migrations repeat across test modules.
Tracking test artifacts collide because tests write to a shared folder instead of isolated directories.
Isolate generated test artifacts into temporary directories for each tracking store test run.
Reuse the shared database cache across all tracking tests to prevent redundant initialization.
search: Tracking store tests must reuse the session-scoped cached_db fixture from tests/conftest.py rather than overriding cached_db in tests/store/tracking/conftest.py. A module-scoped cached_db repeated migrations across modules and used a shared relative artifact_folder that broke per-test artifact isolation. Tests should let tests/store/tracking/conftest.py:store consume the root cached_db with artifacts directed to tmp_path, and any module requiring custom database state must define a new fixture under a distinct name.
